1.title: Table 1. Cohort, tumour, and clinical outcome characteristics (n = 163).
1.note: The table reports demographic, tumour, language, cognitive, and QoL endpoint denominators used to define the analysis samples.

2.title: Table 2. Deficit-related continuous subtest TFNBS summary.
2.note: Values are numbers of significant fs191 ChaCoConn edges. Edge FWE denotes family-wise error correction across edges within each subtest. Across subtests adds Bonferroni correction across the four AAT or five DemTect subtests. The clinical model adjusted for age, WHO grade and log-transformed tumour volume. The location-adjusted model additionally included lesion hemisphere and lesion-volume percentages in frontal, temporal, parietal, occipital, insular and thalamic compartments. The last column lists the two most frequent anatomical group pairs among clinical-model edge-FWE-significant edges, with their edge counts; a dash indicates that no edges were significant.

3.title: Table 3. Exploratory cross-validated prediction models.
3.note: Clinical only: age, WHO grade and log-transformed tumour volume. Clinical + location (baseline): the same predictors plus dominant lobe and lesion hemisphere. Regional extension: baseline plus principal components of 191 regional ChaCo values. Differences are regional minus baseline. Binary endpoints used class-weighted logistic regression; AUC was primary and balanced accuracy secondary. The five continuous DemTect subtests were predicted jointly using multi-output RidgeCV. All models used five-fold cross-validation repeated five times; preprocessing was fitted within each outer training set (Section 2.7). Parentheses contain 95% confidence intervals from 2,000 patient-level bootstrap resamples of averaged out-of-fold predictions. The last three rows show minimum-to-maximum values across the five individual DemTect subtests, not confidence intervals. A dash indicates a measure not reported for that comparison. The training-mean benchmark predicted each subtest using its mean in the corresponding outer training set and yielded a median profile r of {training_mean}; model-minus-benchmark differences were {baseline_vs_mean} for the baseline and {regional_vs_mean} for the regional model. Profile r was calculated across the five subtest scores after scaling by their maxima; the summed-score C-index refers to the sum of raw subtest scores, not the standardised DemTect global score.
